title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Curriculum Induction
interaction: A learned teacher picks reset-controller interventions per stage so that the CMDP student never violates constraints during training.

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration
interaction: The curriculum is over the safety budget itself: PI or Q-learning controllers raise the budget from strict to target during training.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
interaction: A hand-made curriculum over difficulty levels (more hazards; smaller goals) is run with seven safe RL learners; it helps Reacher/Pathway/Height but not Goal.

title: HASARD: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Safe Reinforcement Learning in Embodied Agents
interaction: The HASARD abstract states the benchmark 'features three difficulty levels and two action spaces' and that 'incrementally training across difficulty levels offers an implicit learning curriculum' for its Lagrangian/PID safe RL baselines.

title: SPiDR: A Simple Approach for Zero-Shot Safety in Sim-to-Real Transfer
interaction: Domain randomisation over dynamics is added to the cost constraint as a pessimism penalty from model disagreement.

title: Risk-Averse Model Uncertainty for Distributionally Robust Safe Reinforcement Learning
interaction: Domain randomisation of dynamics is the main baseline for a constrained learner and is beaten when its training distribution is misspecified.

title: Adaptive Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning under Hidden-Parameter Dynamics Shifts
interaction: Constrained learners train on randomised hidden physical parameters and are tested on held-out parameter ranges.

title: Predictive Safety Curricula for Robust Legged Locomotion
interaction: Contexts are allocated by a learned or empirical CVaR of episode safety return (from search snippet; full text unreadable).

title: CurricuVLM: Towards Safe Autonomous Driving via Personalized Safety-Critical Curriculum Learning with Vision-Language Models
interaction: Safety-critical driving scenarios are generated as a curriculum; whether the learner is a CMDP solver was not verified.
